long_biography.plain_text:
A 180-day voyage from France to Shenzhen convinced David Zhong that China could support a wider sailing culture. He had already helped establish one of mainland China's earliest recreational boating clubs, but the long passage exposed him to ports where maritime recreation formed part of everyday urban life. In 2007 he translated that experience into the China Cup International Regatta.

Zhong developed the event through a hybrid model combining government support with professional private operation. The platform expanded beyond racing into boatbuilding, training, club development and event management, with Shenzhen as its base. He also pursued technical standards and licensing structures intended to professionalise domestic sailing. Nearly two decades after the inaugural regatta, he remains chairman of the operating company and continues to direct the event's development.
